ONE BUCKET. SO MANY NEEDS.

A drink. A meal.
A chance to wash.

Imagine sharing a small supply for drinking, cooking and washing. Families need enough safe water for all three. Nobody should have to choose which basic need matters.

🥤 Drinking🍲 Cooking🫧 Washing

Safe drinking water needs clean, covered storage. Used wash water should not go back into it.

LOOK CLOSER

Clear doesn’t always mean safe.

Can you tell whether water is safe just by looking?

The germs in this picture are drawn much bigger so we can see them. Ask a trusted adult about safe drinking water. Learn about safe storage ↗
ONE WATER STORY. MANY LIVES.

It affects all of us.

Not enough water, unsafe water and damaged water systems can have different causes. Their effects reach far beyond the tap.

🏡

Every child deserves a healthy start.

Unsafe water can make people seriously ill and can be deadly. Safe water, toilets and handwashing help protect families. A reliable supply also means less time spent collecting water.

Access is a shared responsibility—not a family’s fault.
REAL FACTS. THE FULL CONTEXT.

Big numbers.
Real people and living things.

These figures describe different places, years and problems. The drought examples are not worldwide annual totals.

CLEAN WATER ACCESS · WORLDWIDE2.1 billion

people lacked safely managed drinking water in 2024.

Safe water should be available when needed, at home, and free from contamination.WHO & UNICEF · 2025 report ↗
HEALTH · GLOBAL ESTIMATE FOR 20191.4 million

deaths could have been prevented with safe water, sanitation and hygiene in 2019.

This includes unsafe drinking water, toilets and hygiene—not only having too little water.World Health Organization ↗
ANIMALS · HORN OF AFRICA DROUGHT13.2 million+

livestock died during the 2020–2023 drought crisis in the Horn of Africa.

This regional crisis involved shortages of water and food for animals. It is not an annual global total.Acted · Horn of Africa response ↗
TREES · TEXAS DROUGHT IN 2011300 million

trees were estimated to have died in the 2011 Texas drought.

This is a historical regional estimate, not a worldwide yearly count.Texas A&M Forest Service ↗
